title: Unit – 4 : Session – 3 : SLO – 2  |  Odd Man Out — Instruction Execution
sections: 1. Group Fetch, Decode, Execute, Store → Store — Fetch, Decode and Execute are the three fundamental stages of the instruction cycle; storing is a sub-step of execution (write-back).
2. Group PC, IR, ALU, CU → ALU — it is the data-processing unit; PC, IR and CU all serve instruction sequencing/control.
3. Group ADD, SUB, MOV, HALT → HALT — it stops the machine; the others are data-processing/transfer instructions that produce a result.
4. Group Register, Cache, RAM, Hard Disk → Hard Disk — it is non-volatile secondary storage; the others are fast volatile storage inside the memory hierarchy.
5. Group Zero Flag, Overflow Flag, Carry Flag, Clock Signal → Clock Signal — it drives timing; the others are ALU status flags.
6. Group Immediate, Direct, Indirect, Parallel → Parallel — it is not an addressing mode; the other three are.
7. Group RISC, CISC, Pipelining, GPU → GPU — it is a hardware device; RISC/CISC are ISA design philosophies and pipelining is an execution technique.
8. Group Branch, Jump, Call, Load → Load — it is a data-transfer instruction; the others alter the control flow.
9. Group Operand Fetch, Instruction Fetch, Write Back, Memory Access → Instruction Fetch — it fetches the instruction word; the others move data between CPU and memory.
10. Group Microoperation, Macrooperation, Nanoperation, Clock Cycle → Nanoperation — it is not a real architectural term; microoperations execute instructions and clock cycles time them.
